skill.name: verification-before-completion
skill.description: Requires fresh verification evidence before claiming work is complete, fixed, passing, or ready for review.
skill.summary: Enforces evidence-based completion claims for coding workflows.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown backtick false positives, but several entries are real command-running instructions for tests, builds, linting, and CLI checks. The skill also contains a protocol-style footer that can steer an agent to inspect CLAUDE.md outside the declared workflow. Publish only with clear command-confirmation guidance and removal of the footer.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running repository commands, especially npm scripts, build tools, and GitHub CLI checks in untrusted workspaces.
Remove the final protocol directive or rewrite it as non-operational documentation that does not instruct agents to inspect CLAUDE.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks delimit a Markdown code fence containing a policy slogan, not executable Ruby or shell code. No command is present in this block.
This finding points at Markdown fence formatting around plain process text. It does not invoke a shell or execute code.

The block tells agents to run full verification commands and lists npm, pytest, go test, make, eslint, tsc, and mypy examples. These are legitimate development checks but can execute project-controlled scripts in untrusted workspaces.
The matched token is a Markdown fence boundary and table setup. The actual command rows are covered by separate findings.

The row instructs agents to run validate-constitution for PRD validation, an external executable whose behavior depends on the local environment. It is a workflow check, but command execution is real.

The row instructs agents to run validate-constitution for epic validation, an external executable whose behavior depends on the local environment. It is legitimate workflow guidance but still executes a command.
The row instructs npm test and npm run build, which execute package scripts from the repository. This is a legitimate verification gate but risky in untrusted projects.
The row instructs npm test and npm run lint, which execute package scripts from the repository. This is useful verification behavior but can run untrusted project code.
The row instructs gh pr checks, which invokes the GitHub CLI and may access repository or account context. It is legitimate release verification but still uses an external tool.
The code fence starts an example completion-evidence template. It documents how to report results and does not execute a command.
The inline npm test text appears inside an evidence-template example, not as a direct command execution step. The run-command behavior is already covered by earlier workflow findings.
The matched token is a Markdown fence boundary before a prose integration section. It does not contain executable code.
The YAML-style block instructs agents to run each required command fresh, which is command execution guidance. It is generic and contextual, so confidence is lower than for explicit commands.
The matched token is Markdown formatting between two documentation examples. No concrete shell command is present at this location.

The task-completion YAML instructs agents to run task-specific tests, which can execute repository-defined commands. The instruction is legitimate verification guidance, but it is still external-command behavior.

content.value_statement: AI agents can overstate completion when tests or builds have not been checked. This skill enforces fresh verification evidence before claims, commits, or pull requests.
actual_capabilities: Requires a verification command before completion claims.
Prompts fresh test, build, lint, or type-check execution.
Defines success criteria using exit codes and output evidence.
Provides a concise evidence format for completion messages.
Maps development flow gates to required verification checks.
limitations: Does not discover project-specific commands automatically.
Depends on local tools, scripts, and repository setup.
Cannot guarantee that tests cover every acceptance criterion.
Long or destructive commands still require user judgment.

use_cases.title: Confirm a Code Fix
use_cases.description: Require fresh test or build evidence before an assistant says a bug is fixed.

use_cases.title: Enforce Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Make each workflow stage show command output before moving to the next stage.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect clear verification results before commits, pull requests, or release handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Verify A Simple Fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check after a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before you claim this fix is complete, identify the verification command, run it fresh, and summarize the result with the exit code.

prompt_templates.title: Check A Build Claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that the project still builds. Run the relevant build command, inspect the output, and report only evidence-backed conclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Commit Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Before preparing a commit, run the relevant tests, lint checks, and build checks. Report failures, skipped checks, and exact evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Gate A Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: For this release gate, identify every required verification check, run each one fresh, and explain whether the release can proceed.

output_examples.input: The assistant finished a bug fix and wants to say it is done.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the relevant test command, runs it fresh, checks the exit code, and reports passing evidence before claiming completion.

output_examples.input: A build claim is needed before opening a pull request.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs the build check, reviews the output, and states whether the result supports the pull request claim.

output_examples.input: A workflow stage is ready to close.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists required checks, records which checks passed or failed, and blocks completion when evidence is missing.

best_practices: Run verification commands after the final change, not before it.
Report exit codes, failure counts, and skipped checks clearly.
Ask for confirmation before running commands in untrusted repositories.
anti_patterns: Claiming tests pass without fresh command output.
Using cached or earlier results as current evidence.
Treating a small change as exempt from verification.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to identify and run relevant verification commands when appropriate. User confirmation may still be required.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it choose the right command for every project?
faq.answer: No. It uses common patterns, but project-specific commands must come from repository documentation or user guidance.

faq.question: Does it prove a feature is correct?
faq.answer: No. It improves evidence discipline, but test quality and acceptance coverage still matter.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted codebases?
faq.answer: Use caution. Verification commands can execute repository scripts, so confirm commands before running them in untrusted workspaces.

faq.question: What should completion evidence include?
faq.answer: It should include the command purpose, exit result, important output summary, and any failures or skipped checks.
